requirements.evidence: All contract routes exist with the right names and middleware (routes/web.php:21-57: guest login/register, auth logout, auth+verified home, throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed verification.verify). Login uses lowercase e-mail+IP key, 5 tries, auth.failed/auth.throttle on email, session()->regenerate() and redirectIntended(route('home')) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:31-57). Register uses str()->transliterate('register|'.$ip), Password::defaults() with 'confirmed', fires Registered, logs in and regenerates (Register.php:46-72). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (NewPasswordController.php:33-39). VerifyEmailController compares the route id to the logged-in user and returns 403 (VerifyEmailController.php:18-26). Locale pins are in phpunit.xml:22-23 and .env.example. Problem: AppServiceProvider.php:33 adds Event::listen(Registered::class, SendEmailVerificationNotification::class), but the framework's EventServiceProvider already registers that listener, so registration probably sends the verification mail twice. Small slips: the forgot-password page title is __('ui.login') (forgot-password.blade.php:1), and welcome.blade.php still hardcodes 'Bulma CSS'.

conventions.evidence: Livewire components use #[Validate] + $this->validate() (Login.php:12-16, Register.php:16-20). Views use route() everywhere, and a test checks every view for hardcoded href/action. Inputs use plain wire:model. User keeps its #[Fillable]. Docs are kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md, README.md 'Autenticação' table). Deviations: User::create is called directly in the component (Register.php:58) rather than through an app/Actions class. The layout loads Bulma from a CDN as a fallback (layouts/app.blade.php:16) instead of relying only on the project's Vite build.

security.evidence: Session is regenerated on login and register. Logout invalidates the session and regenerates the token (LogoutController.php:13-16). Forgot-password always returns passwords.sent (PasswordResetLinkController.php:24-27). The verification link is bound to the authenticated user via hash_equals on id and hash. Output is escaped with {{ }} everywhere, and remember_token is rotated on reset. Gaps with limited impact: Register only calls RateLimiter::hit after a successful create (Register.php:66), so failed submissions are never throttled and the unique:users,email rule can be used to enumerate e-mails without limit. The CDN stylesheet is loaded without SRI (layouts/app.blade.php:16).

tests.evidence: Five new Pest files cover login (success, intended URL, failure, lockout, strict e-mail), the home/guest/unverified redirects, logout, registration (happy path, confirmed, the password rule dataset, unique, throttle), password reset (no enumeration, 429 on the 7th request, single email input, remember_token rotation, PasswordReset event, invalid token, weak password), verification (tampered id gives 403, another user's link, resend, already verified), and localization (pt_BR/en, .env.example, phpunit.xml, no hardcoded links). Weaker spots: the lockout test asserts only assertHasErrors(['email']), not the auth.throttle message (AuthenticationTest.php:97). No test would catch the duplicate verification mail, because Notification::assertSentTo passes even when the mail is sent twice. The logout test does not check that the CSRF token is regenerated.

simplicity.evidence: The controllers are small and use the framework's Password broker. Some code is redundant: the Login/Register mount() redirects when Auth::check() (Login.php:21-26) even though the routes already use the guest middleware. TestCase::setUp forces the pt_BR locale (tests/TestCase.php:9-19), which duplicates the phpunit.xml pin and hides whether that pin works. The Event::listen line duplicates a framework default.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods short, with consistent Bulma markup across views and comments only where they help (PasswordResetLinkController.php:26, AppServiceProvider.php:35). Minor: Register mixes a #[Validate] attribute with a rules() method for the password, and its throttle message reuses the login-specific auth.throttle text ('Muitas tentativas de login') (Register.php:49-51).

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Unrelated edits: the bootstrap/providers.php import refactor, the quote/newline changes in lang/pt_BR/{auth,pagination,passwords,validation}.php, the new route names 'welcome' and 'bulma-test', and the <span> changed to <strong> in welcome.blade.php. Enabling RefreshDatabase in tests/Pest.php is justified by the new DB-backed tests.

issues.explanation: Laravel's EventServiceProvider already wires Registered to SendEmailVerificationNotification, so registering it again in AppServiceProvider probably sends every new user two verification e-mails, and the tests cannot catch it.
The registration limiter is only hit after a successful account creation, so failed attempts (including e-mail probes against unique:users,email) are never throttled.
The layout falls back to Bulma 0.9.4 from a third-party CDN without SRI instead of relying on the project's Vite assets.
The lockout test only asserts that some e-mail error exists, not the required auth.throttle message.
Forcing the pt_BR locale in TestCase::setUp duplicates the phpunit.xml pin and hides whether that pin works.
The forgot-password page title uses __('ui.login') instead of a forgot-password label.
'Bulma CSS' is still hardcoded text, against the rule that screen text comes from translation files.
The registration lockout reuses the login-specific auth.throttle message ('Muitas tentativas de login').
The user is created directly in the component rather than through an app/Actions class, the project's pattern for writes.
The provider-import refactor and the lang file quote/newline reformatting are unrelated to the task.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, password reset, signed e-mail verification, pt-BR translations) with good tests and matching docs, and nearly the whole contract is met. It needs changes before merging: the manually registered Registered listener most likely doubles the verification e-mails, and registration throttling only counts successful sign-ups. The rest are small issues: a CDN fallback, a wrong page title, a weak lockout assertion and a few unrelated edits.
